claims.title: Lapita settlement of New Caledonia
claims.summary: Austronesian voyagers of the Lapita culture reached the archipelago, establishing the earliest human presence and leaving the dentate-stamped pottery first studied at the New Caledonian site that gives the culture its name.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of New Caledonia: Kanaky / Nouvelle-Calédonie — an Austronesian-settled Pacific archipelago, a French colony and penal bagne built on the world's richest nickel, now a sui generis collectivity working through one of the planet's last formal decolonisation processes.", terralore.co/country/NCL/chronicle#ev-1000bce-lapita-settlement-of-new-caledonia, claim TL:NCL:event:1000bce:lapita-settlement-of-new-caledonia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Emergence of the Kanak
claims.summary: Successive waves of Melanesian migrants intermarried with the Lapita settlers, giving rise to the Kanak, the Melanesian people indigenous to New Caledonia, with a clan-based society organised around chiefs, yam cultivation and ancestral land.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of New Caledonia: Kanaky / Nouvelle-Calédonie — an Austronesian-settled Pacific archipelago, a French colony and penal bagne built on the world's richest nickel, now a sui generis collectivity working through one of the planet's last formal decolonisation processes.", terralore.co/country/NCL/chronicle#ev-500bce-emergence-of-the-kanak, claim TL:NCL:event:500bce:emergence-of-the-kanak, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cook names New Caledonia
claims.summary: The British explorer James Cook landed at Balade on the east coast and named the territory New Caledonia after the classical name for Scotland, marking the first recorded European contact.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of New Caledonia: Kanaky / Nouvelle-Calédonie — an Austronesian-settled Pacific archipelago, a French colony and penal bagne built on the world's richest nickel, now a sui generis collectivity working through one of the planet's last formal decolonisation processes.", terralore.co/country/NCL/chronicle#ev-1774-cook-names-new-caledonia, claim TL:NCL:event:1774:cook-names-new-caledonia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sandalwood traders and missionaries arrive
claims.summary: From the 1840s sandalwood traders and Christian missionaries — Protestant and, from 1843, French Catholic Marists — established themselves among the Kanak, bringing trade goods, conversion, firearms and epidemic disease.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of New Caledonia: Kanaky / Nouvelle-Calédonie — an Austronesian-settled Pacific archipelago, a French colony and penal bagne built on the world's richest nickel, now a sui generis collectivity working through one of the planet's last formal decolonisation processes.", terralore.co/country/NCL/chronicle#ev-1840-sandalwood-traders-and-missionaries-arrive, claim TL:NCL:event:1840:sandalwood-traders-and-missionaries-arrive, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: France annexes New Caledonia
claims.summary: Rear Admiral Febvrier-Despointes took possession of the archipelago for France, beginning formal colonial rule and pre-empting British ambitions in the region.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of New Caledonia: Kanaky / Nouvelle-Calédonie — an Austronesian-settled Pacific archipelago, a French colony and penal bagne built on the world's richest nickel, now a sui generis collectivity working through one of the planet's last formal decolonisation processes.", terralore.co/country/NCL/chronicle#ev-1853-france-annexes-new-caledonia, claim TL:NCL:event:1853:france-annexes-new-caledonia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Penal colony established
claims.summary: France made New Caledonia a penal settlement, transporting tens of thousands of convicts — including Communards after 1871 — whose forced labour helped build the colonial economy until transportation ended in the 1890s.

claims.title: The revolt of Ataï
claims.summary: The high chief Ataï led a major Kanak insurrection against land dispossession; the rising killed about 200 colonists and gendarmes and was crushed at the cost of roughly a thousand Kanak lives, with Ataï killed and his head sent to Paris.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of New Caledonia: Kanaky / Nouvelle-Calédonie — an Austronesian-settled Pacific archipelago, a French colony and penal bagne built on the world's richest nickel, now a sui generis collectivity working through one of the planet's last formal decolonisation processes.", terralore.co/country/NCL/chronicle#ev-1878-the-revolt-of-atai, claim TL:NCL:event:1878:the-revolt-of-atai, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Nickel mining begins
claims.summary: The Société Le Nickel began industrial exploitation of New Caledonia's nickel — among the largest deposits in the world — making mining the economic engine that drew settlers and accelerated Kanak dispossession.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of New Caledonia: Kanaky / Nouvelle-Calédonie — an Austronesian-settled Pacific archipelago, a French colony and penal bagne built on the world's richest nickel, now a sui generis collectivity working through one of the planet's last formal decolonisation processes.", terralore.co/country/NCL/chronicle#ev-1880-nickel-mining-begins, claim TL:NCL:event:1880:nickel-mining-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: FLNKS founded
claims.summary: Pro-independence parties united in the Kanak and Socialist National Liberation Front (FLNKS) under Jean-Marie Tjibaou, demanding sovereignty for a country it called Kanaky and opening the most intense phase of the independence struggle.

claims.title: Re-inscribed on the UN decolonisation list
claims.summary: The UN General Assembly re-inscribed New Caledonia on its list of Non-Self-Governing Territories, formally recognising the Kanak people's right to self-determination and placing the territory back on the UN decolonisation agenda.

claims.title: Ouvéa cave crisis
claims.summary: FLNKS militants killed four gendarmes and seized hostages in a cave on Ouvéa; a French military assault on 5 May freed the hostages but left nineteen Kanak dead, a tragedy that became a turning point toward negotiation.

claims.title: Matignon Accords
claims.summary: The French state, FLNKS and RPCR signed the Matignon Accords, ending les Événements, dividing the territory into three provinces and scheduling a self-determination referendum for 1998.

claims.title: Nouméa Accord signed
claims.summary: The Nouméa Accord set out a gradual, declared-irreversible transfer of powers, recognition of Kanak identity and up to three referendums on full sovereignty, making New Caledonia a sui generis collectivity within the French Republic.

claims.title: Accord ratified by referendum
claims.summary: New Caledonian voters approved the Nouméa Accord by about 72%, and its provisions were written into the French Constitution (Articles 76–77).

claims.summary: UNESCO inscribes the Lagoons of New Caledonia for reef diversity and intact ecosystems — the territory's other inheritance, held in common by both of its political camps.

claims.title: First independence referendum
claims.summary: In the first Nouméa Accord referendum, voters chose to remain part of France by about 56.7% to 43.3%, with the independence vote concentrated among the Kanak.

claims.title: Second independence referendum
claims.summary: Independence was again rejected, but by a narrower margin of about 53.3% to 46.7%, a closing gap that sharpened the political contest.

claims.title: Third referendum and Kanak boycott
claims.summary: The final referendum rejected independence by about 96% to 4%, but turnout was only ~44%: pro-independence parties and most Kanak voters boycotted after France declined to postpone the vote, and the two sides drew opposite conclusions about its legitimacy.

claims.title: Deadly unrest over electoral reform
claims.summary: A French move to widen the provincial electorate — feared to dilute the Kanak vote — triggered the worst violence in decades from 13 May: fourteen dead, some €2 billion in damage and a state of emergency.

claims.title: Bougival agreement
claims.summary: France and most local parties signed the Bougival agreement proposing a "State of New Caledonia" within the Republic with a Caledonian nationality; the pro-independence FLNKS rejected it and the ratifying referendum was delayed, leaving the territory's status unresolved into 2026.

claims.title: Nickel, still the ground everyone stands on
claims.summary: Through the unrest and its aftermath the territory mined 116,000 tonnes of nickel in 2024 and an estimated 140,000 in 2025 — one of the largest outputs on earth, and the revenue any future status has to be paid for out of.
